articles.title: 1Password Security Incident
articles.raw_description: 1Password identified a security incident involving some of our backend systems. Customer vaults were not accessed and remain secure. by 1Password November 25, 2026 - 4 min Related Categories Security What happened On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers. This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker. What information was affected The attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users. These records include: Names and email addresses Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times Public keys (which are public by design, this has no impact to user security) Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (which cannot be used to access your account) Tokens present in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery Other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture (e.g. version numeric identifiers, file numeric identifiers) The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system. Our source code is not customer data, and contains no user secrets. CI/CD

articles.title: A few questions for the guy who went snorkeling in a Home Depot retention pond
articles.raw_description: He found it teeming with life and beauty. Down to Earth A few questions for the guy who went snorkeling in a Home Depot retention pond He found it teeming with life and beauty. by Neel Dhanesha Nov 25, 2026, 12:00 PM UTC Share Joseph Ricketts in the retention pond. Joseph Ricketts Neel Dhanesha is a senior writer at Vox, covering biodiversity loss and climate change. Previously, he was a staff writer at the Nieman Journalism Lab at Harvard and helped launch the climate news site Heatmap. One night earlier this fall, a biologist and YouTuber in Florida named Joseph Ricketts went snorkeling in a retention pond next to his local Home Depot. He filmed what he saw and posted a video to his channel titled “ Night Snorkel In a Home Depot Retention Pond .” It quickly blew up, hitting more than 2 million views as of this writing, and for good reason: It’s not at all what you might expect. Ricketts found an aquatic world teeming with life on his dive into what is, from the surface, a stagnant pool of water filled with old beer cans. A water snake undulated through the pond, a bulge in its stomach revealing a recent meal. Tadpoles darted about, some of them half on their way to froghood. Mysterious shrimp scuttled along the silty bottom. Ricketts, who works as a crocodile and alligator research biologist in Florida, went for his first snorkeling trip when he was 16 years old. articles.title: Much shorter version of GRH Lean verification from Anthropic
articles.raw_description: A short Lean 4 proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis - lsernau/grh-lean GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, in Lean 4 Research artifact. Not maintained and not accepting contributions. A Lean 4 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, built on Mathlib and using only the axioms propext , Classical.choice and Quot.sound . The proof is based on Levent Alpöge's, with Claude ( https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf ). This repository is a shorter version, produced in collaboration with my colleagues at Anthropic, and Claude. Two editions grh/ : readable edition, about 300,000 lines. Start at grh/GUIDE.md . grh-compact/ : the same five theorems, about 76,000 lines. Each folder is its own Lake project with its own README. Build Needs Lean v4.35.0 and Mathlib at commit 56a00585. In either folder: lake exe cache get lake build lake env lean scripts/PrintAxioms.lean A build takes one to two hours on 12 cores with 24 GB of memory (about 85 minutes more if the Mathlib cache is missing). Status The proof has passed machine checks only, listed in each folder's README. No mathematician has read it through, and no paper comes with it. License Apache 2.0, Copyright 2026 Anthropic, PBC. See LICENSE , and NOTICE and ATTRIBUTION.md in each folder.

articles.title: GPT-6.2 Astra is the first model to beat Googlers' code golf records
articles.raw_description: Back in 2015, when I was still at Google, there was a small group of code-golf enthusiasts spending hours trying to save just one byte on their solutions for weekly code-golf problems. No matter how hard you tried, there always seemed to be another Googler who found a shorter solution. And once a problem entered the challenge phase and every solution became public, it was always astonishing to read how brilliant other people's solutions were. 11 years later, LLMs are evolving fast. A recent OpenAI post ("Perplexity and Intelligence", https://openai.com/index/perplexity-and-intelligence/ ) described researchers watching a model solve open math problems one after another in a Slack thread. I started to wonder: how would frontier models compete with the records that a small group of brilliant minds created with hours of effort each week? So I built this benchmark. Frontier models do find a lot of new approaches (and very brilliant ones) to solve these problems. For example, in two problems ("Surviving Queens" and "The Rolling Dice"), frontier models use complex numbers to solve them in Python and Ruby (both languages have built-in complex number support). And for the "(-5)-Smooth Numbers" problem, where you have to write code to list the first n positive integers of the form (-2)^x⋅(-3)^y⋅(-5)^z, most solutions build them with nested loops or by growing a set, then sort. articles.raw_description: The NYT doesn’t want AI metadata inadvertently added to its photos. AI News Tech The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features An email sent to freelance photographers says Photoshop’s latest update uses AI ‘in ways that may not be apparent.’ An email sent to freelance photographers says Photoshop’s latest update uses AI ‘in ways that may not be apparent.’ by Emma Roth Nov 24, 2026, 4:09 PM UTC Link Share Gift Photo: Marcin Golba / NurPhoto via Getty Images Emma Roth is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO. The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI “in ways that may not be apparent to users.” In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads , two of the Times ’ photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, write that the use of these features “can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated.” Adobe has spent the past few years filling Photoshop and other apps in its creative suite with a trove of AI-powered tools. The November update cited by the NYT ’s email adds several new AI features, including Adobe’s new “AI Assisted Editor” view , which lets users access all of Photoshop’s AI features from a single toolbar. articles.title: Tell HN: Lots of Ask HNs again
articles.raw_description: There have been questions about why the /ask page ( https://news.ycombinator.com/ask ) was running dry of Ask HNs - e.g.: Ask HN: Why is Ask HN only showing me 14 posts? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49984484 - Oct 2026 (47 comments) Ask HN: Why is pagination gone on "Ask HN", and showing only 19 items? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50280719 - Oct 2026 (3 comments) I believe I found the problem. The pool of stories for https://news.ycombinator.com/ask has traditionally been drawn from the ranked stories list from which we generate the frontpage. That list is restricted to the top 1500 ranked submissions, and it seems the % of submissions which are text posts (i.e. no linked URL) had declined enough to starve the Ask HN feed. The solution is to compute a separate list of ranked Ask HNs. p.s. "Ask HN" is the conventional name but it means text posts. The title can also start with "Tell HN" or nothing in particular. They're just posts which were submitted without a URL.

articles.title: パスワード管理「1Password」でデータ流出、一部顧客の氏名やメールアドレスなど／パスワード保管庫やその鍵は無事、招待・復旧メールを装ったフィッシングに注意
articles.raw_description: 加AgileBitsは11月25日（現地時間、以下同）、パスワード管理サービス「1Password」のバックエンドシステムの一部が不正アクセスを受け、一部顧客の氏名やメールアドレスなどが流出したと発表した。同社によると、ユーザーのパスワード保管庫（Vault）の中身や、それを保護する鍵への影響はなかった。 ニュース パスワード管理「1Password」でデータ流出、一部顧客の氏名やメールアドレスなど パスワード保管庫やその鍵は無事、招待・復旧メールを装ったフィッシングに注意 樽井 秀人 2026年11月26日 07:55 「1Password」の公式ブログ 加AgileBitsは11月25日（現地時間、以下同）、パスワード管理サービス「1Password」のバックエンドシステムの一部が不正アクセスを受け、一部顧客の氏名やメールアドレスなどが流出したと発表した。同社によると、ユーザーのパスワード保管庫（Vault）の中身や、それを保護する鍵への影響はなかった。 同社は11月19日、従業員の企業用「GitHub」アカウントに攻撃者がアクセスした形跡があるとして調査を開始。攻撃者がこのアカウントを使ってソースコードにアクセスしてバックエンドサービスへ悪意あるコードをプッシュしたほか、顧客に関する管理データをダウンロードしたことが判明した。攻撃者が持ち出したアカウント記録には、以下の情報が含まれる。 氏名とメールアドレス アカウントとユーザーの識別子、アカウントの作成日時と最終サインイン日時 公開鍵（設計上公開されているもので、ユーザーのセキュリティには影響しない） Secure Remote Password（SRP）プロトコルのパラメーター（アカウントへのアクセスには利用できない） 招待、プロビジョニング、アカウント復旧に関する一部のメールのリンクに含まれるトークン バージョンやファイルの識別番号など、アカウントに関する機密性のない内部メタデータ さらに攻撃者は、非公開リポジトリのソースコードをコピーし、開発・配布に使うCI/CDシステムにもアクセスしていた。ソースコードに顧客データやユーザーの秘密情報は含まれなかったが、同社は侵入経路を遮断し、漏洩した可能性のある内部認証情報を交換または失効させたという。封じ込めと復旧措置の検証は外部の専門家に依頼しており、アプリとサービスは通常どおり稼働しているとのこと。 なお、流出した招待・復旧用のトークンだけではアカウントにアクセスできないが、念のため、確認コードを数字6桁から英数字10文字へ変更して推測を難しくするなどの対策がとられたという。該当する少数のユーザーには個別に通知済みで、流出したプロビジョニング用トークンによるアカウント乗っ取りの証拠は見つかっていないとしている。 We’re sharing an update about a recent security incident involving some of 1Password’s backend systems.
